title: Formal methods in metaphysics: mereology, plural and higher-order logic, hyperintensionality
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
purpose: Learn the formal tools of current metaphysics: ground mereology and classical extensional mereology and their alternatives, plural logic and plural quantification, second-order and higher-order logic, counterpart theory and the logic of identity, impossible worlds and hyperintensionality, and the logic of grounding, with small Python models for checking claims.

weeks.1: Mereology: parthood axioms and ground mereology
weeks.2: Classical extensional mereology: sums and extensionality
weeks.3: Finite models of mereology in Python
weeks.4: Alternatives: gunk, junk and non-extensional mereology
weeks.5: Plural logic: plural reference and quantification
weeks.8: Counterpart theory and the logic of identity
weeks.11: Formal methods in practice: a case study

blocks.deliverable: Prove five theorems of ground mereology.
Check mereological axioms in finite models with code.
Translate ten plural sentences into plural logic.
Week 7 midterm; prove a result in counterpart theory.
Build an impossible-worlds model for a hyperintensional claim.
Formalize and test an argument from a recent paper.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Formal analysis: take one argument from a recent metaphysics paper, formalize it in the appropriate logic (mereology, plural or higher-order logic, counterpart theory or a logic of grounding), prove the valid steps, build models by hand or in Python that test the questionable premises, and write a 3,000-word analysis of what the formalization shows.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
